high_consensus.description: This is a real release blocker disguised as a TODO. Adding a hard merge gate for unresolved pricing values is low effort and directly protects FR-3 and cost-ledger correctness.
Excellent operational hardening item. Missing/corrupt/stale cache handling is a common runtime path, and explicit behavior here prevents undefined request-time failures.

Important and domain-correct concern: cost-cap enforcement is concurrency-sensitive. Specifying async-safe locking and in-flight budget semantics adds complexity but is worth it for cost-control integrity.
High-impact gap: fallback behavior for 429/5xx is central to reliability and currently ambiguous. Clarifying this will materially improve runtime resilience in common failure modes.

blockers.concern: Alias retarget precedence is counterintuitive: `prefer_pro_models` can overwrite explicit user alias overrides unless denylisted, increasing surprise and incident risk.
blockers.why_matters: Operators typically expect explicit user overrides to be highest precedence. Current semantics can unintentionally route critical workloads to expensive or behaviorally different models.
blockers.location: Sections 5.9 and 5.10: Tier-group application and precedence
blockers.recommendation: Invert precedence so explicit user alias overrides win by default, and add an explicit `force_retarget` list for opt-in aggressive behavior.

blockers.concern: Default `strict` behavior for unknown `/v1/responses` shapes creates a single-vendor contract fragility that can trigger production-wide failures when OpenAI adds new output types.
blockers.why_matters: Provider-side response evolution is common. Failing loud is safe for correctness but can still halt all traffic unexpectedly, especially with no auto-canary mechanism.
blockers.recommendation: Introduce staged rollout policy: default to strict in CI and canary, degrade in production with alerting, plus automated fixture capture for unknown types and a feature flag with expiry.

blockers.concern: Per-session cost cap is not globally enforced across multi-process workflows unless operators manually align `trace_id` and shared ledger usage.
blockers.why_matters: Real Loa runs may fork/parallelize. Independent process caps can multiply spend far beyond intended safety limits, undermining FR-5a financial guardrails.
blockers.recommendation: Define a mandatory shared budget scope (run_id/session_id) propagated automatically across subprocesses; fail closed when cap configured but shared coordination is unavailable.

blockers.concern: Probe cache trust checks rely on file owner/mode assumptions that may fail in containers, CI runners, or shared volumes, causing fallback logic to silently degrade to UNKNOWN behavior.
blockers.why_matters: Security hardening can accidentally become reliability regression. If trust checks fail often in valid deployments, fallback chain becomes ineffective during outages.
blockers.recommendation: Specify deployment-compatible trust model (UID namespaces, container users), add signed cache or checksum-based integrity, and expose health status when trust checks disable fallback.

blockers.concern: Strict `endpoint_family` validation can hard-fail upgraded operator environments with custom OpenAI model entries, and the compatibility env fallback has no enforced sunset or telemetry.
blockers.why_matters: A config-load failure on first run after upgrade is an operational outage. The stopgap (`LOA_LEGACY_ENDPOINT_FAMILY_DEFAULT=chat`) may become permanent hidden debt because there is no removal trigger or migration tracking.
blockers.location: Section 3.4: Endpoint family strict validation + operator-migration backstop
blockers.recommendation: Add explicit deprecation lifecycle: warning counter metrics, CI check for fallback usage, hard removal version, and a pre-upgrade validator command that blocks rollout until custom configs are migrated.
